candidates.title: UPS shield logo refused copyright registration: 'insufficiently creative'
candidates.claim: US Copyright Office Review Board affirmed refusal to register two UPS brown-and-gold shield logos (shield alone; shield with lowercase lettering): familiar geometric shapes, conventional gradient, ordinary lettering, 'insufficiently creative'; protection turns on 'the resulting expression rather than the effort or decisions involved'. Commercial recognition 'does not necessarily establish' copyright eligibility. Decision does not address UPS's trademark rights.
candidates.verification: Cross-checked: Law360 (2026-11-02, Adam Lidgett, paywalled summary: 'weren't creative enough'); Business Insurance (2026-11-03, citing TFL). Board decision text itself not read (linked from Law360, paywalled). Context: previous shield designed 1961 by Paul Rand, redesigned 2003 (Truck News 2003-03-26).

lenses_summary.verification_red_team: C1: three outlets agree on the core fact (Review Board affirmed refusal, 'not creative enough'); TFL gives the board's reasoning and quotes. Board PDF not read directly: say 'the US copyright office refused', not quote paragraph numbers. It is a COPYRIGHT registration ruling only; it says nothing about trademark: never say 'UPS lost its logo' or 'anyone can copy it'. Not legal advice; one board decision, no precedential weight (per TFL). Paul Rand 1961 / 2003 redesign context from Truck News 2003. C2 lacks percentages; C9 and C10 are 2025 or headline-only; C12 unread.
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Owners believe a logo is worth more if it is clever, detailed and 'creative', and pay for complexity. The ruling flips that: one of the most recognised marks in the world is legally 'ordinary shapes', and its value came from decades of being seen on every truck and box. Relief + challenge: you don't need a genius mark, you need a simple one you will repeat for years.
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Pure identity strategy, the studio's core service; gives a designer's honest opinion ('simple is not weak; recognition is earned by use'), works identically for Persian and international audiences (UPS is globally known; no regional naming needed). Commercial bridge: design brief and consistency, not legal promises.

gates.brand_fit_gate: C1 passes. C10, C12 fail repeat/verification; C6 low relevance; C3, C5 low reach.
gates.story_gate: C1: tension = 'too plain to be called creative, too famous to mistake'; concrete image = a plain brown parcel with a simple shield, seen a billion times. Beats C9 (good tension, stale verification) and C4 (weak tension).

decision.why: Fresh (ruling 30 Oct, reported 2-3 Nov), verified by three outlets, globally recognisable, directly useful to every owner briefing a logo, and not a repeat of the last 7 days (distinct from 11-05 memory and 11-04 visibility: this is about where a mark's value comes from).
